text:
maria: kicking off a shadow bringup for the new quantized variant (q4_0-lite) of our onboarding model. running a 30m shadow traffic sweep against dedicated pool A. low risk, read-only. sharing initial numbers in a bit.
aj: saw p50 ~ stable but p99 jumped ~180ms at qps 220, curious if it's burst/kvcache warmup. any loadgen config?
maria: loadgen config pasted below\n```
profile: steady_ramp
qps: 220
concurrency: auto
sequence_len: 512
batch_window_ms: 8
kv_prefetch: true
```
\nkai: got the logs from the runner during the spike, looks like batch formation went from ~8ms -> ~30ms for a subset of requests, likely due to a small number of long sequences being scheduled in the same window. attaching snippet:
```
2026-03-20T14:02:11Z runner[pid=88] batch_window=8ms formed_batch=256 tokens=13000 latency_ms=32
2026-03-20T14:02:12Z runner[pid=88] batch_window=8ms formed_batch=16 tokens=400 latency_ms=6
```
aj: interesting — formed_batch variance is huge. could be ordering or the new q4 kernels causing slower kernel init for some shapes?
maria: perf-bot posted the numeric compare for token cost and latency: cost/token down ~14% but avg latency down only 3% and tail worse.
perf-bot: shadow report: cost_per_token: "0.00093 -> 0.00080"; p50_latency_ms: "45 -> 44"; p95_latency_ms: "112 -> 160"; p99_latency_ms: "210 -> 380"
devon: also ran a quick quality check — a tiny regression on factuality for the KB QA subset (precision drop 0.6 pts). sample: expected "Q3 revenue 2024: $12.1M" model returned "$12.9M" in 3/200 examples. not huge but worth tracking.
maria: thanks. so tradeoff: cost down but tail latency and a small quality regression. we need to decide go/no-go for canary. thoughts?
kai: propose we try two quick experiments: 1) increase batch_window_ms to 12ms to let the kernel shape stabilize, 2) enable kvcache-prefetch only after warmup (delay first 50 reqs). both are config-level and reversible.
aj: agree. also add a temporary routing policy to limit concurrency to 48 for the canary to protect p99. we should run a concurrency sweep: [16, 32, 48, 64] and capture latency+cost.
maria: i can push a canary with those configs to dedicated pool A in ~15m. CI gating note: our CI perf job didn't catch the p99 because its load shape uses short sequences (64 tokens). we should add a 512-token job.
ci-bot: scheduled job "perf/long-seq-canary" (owner: @maria) to run after deploy, expected duration 35m.
devon: also propose we add a simple quality_regression_rate metric to the eval harness (binary pass/fail on the KB QA examples) and emit alerts if >0.5% regression.
maria: added to list. action items: (1) canary w/ batch_window=12 + delayed-kv-prefetch, concurrency cap 48, run perf/long-seq-canary (ci-bot) (2) run the concurrency sweep and post the perf-bot summary (3) add quality_regression_rate to eval harness and wire alert. anyone want to pick one?
aj: i'll own the concurrency sweep and dashboard wiring.
kai: i'll run the two config experiments and collect runner logs.
devon: i'll add the quality metric and a simple CI check.
maria: thanks team. will post results here. for visibility @eng-ml @eng-platform. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: deploy to dedicated-pool-A started (id=deploy-7892)
maria: quick note — if we still see p99 issues after batch_window bump, fallback plan is to serve the previous fp16 variant for canary traffic and continue q4 experiments in isolated load tests.
aj: ack.
perf-bot: scheduled report incoming in ~40m. expected outputs: cost delta table, latency histogram (16/32/48/64), quality_regression_rate trend.
maria: leaving this thread open until canary results in case anyone wants to add logs/samples.
